paper.title: Generalized Linear Bandits with Local Differential Privacy

settings.name_in_paper: Single-parameter linear contextual bandit under LDP
unmapped: (epsilon,delta)-local differential privacy constraint on user-to-server messages (privacy delta is distinct from the failure probability)
per-arm feature vectors x_{t,a} drawn i.i.d. over rounds satisfying eigenvalue conditions (Assumptions 2,3: kappa_u, kappa_l, p_*)
the learner knows the privacy level delta and the bounds C_B (context norm) and c_r (reward bound) used to calibrate privacy noise
settings.definition_quote:
The user in round $t$ with context $X_t\in\R^d$ receives (processed) historical information $S_{t-1}$ from the server, and chooses an action $a_t\in [K]$ to obtain a random reward $r_t = v(X_t, a_t) + \epsilon_t$ . 
Define $\mathcal{F}_t$ as the filtration of all historical information up to time $t$, i.e., $\mathcal{F}_t = \sigma(X_1, \cdots, X_t, \epsilon_1,\cdots, \epsilon_{t-1})$, and we require $\E[\epsilon_t\lvert \mathcal{F}_t ] = 0,\E[\exp( \lambda\epsilon_t)\lvert \mathcal{F}_t ]\leq\exp(\dfrac{\sigma_\epsilon^2\lambda^2}{2}),\forall\lambda\in\R $.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-parameter generalized linear contextual bandit under LDP
unmapped: epsilon-local differential privacy constraint on user-to-server messages
per-arm feature vectors drawn i.i.d. satisfying eigenvalue conditions (Assumptions 2,3: kappa_u, kappa_l, p_*)
the learner knows kappa_l, p_* (step size eta_t = c' d/(kappa_l zeta p_* t)) and the bounds C_B, c_r
settings.definition_quote: We consider the generalized linear bandits by allowing $v(X_t, a_t) = \mu(X_t^T\theta^{\star}_{a_t})$, where $\mu:\R\to \R$ is a link function and $\theta^{\star}_i\in\R^d$ is the underlying parameter of the $i$-th arm.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-parameter linear contextual bandit under epsilon-LDP, K=2 Gaussian contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: epsilon-local differential privacy constraint on all messages used by the algorithm
settings.definition_quote:
For $\theta\in\R^d$ and an algorithm $\pi$, we denote $\E[\text{Reg}_{\pi}(T;\theta)]$ the expectation regret of $\pi$ when the underlying parameter is $\theta$. When $K = 2$ and $x_{t,a}\sim \mathcal{N}(0,I_d/d)$ are independent over $a\in [K]$, we have for any possible $\varepsilon$-LDP algorithm \textcolor{black}{$\pi$}, $
		  \sup_{\theta^{\star}:\lVert \theta^{\star}\rVert_2\leq 1 }\E[\text{Reg}_{\textcolor{black}{\pi}}(T;\theta^{\star})] = \Omega(\sqrt{T}/\varepsilon).
		$

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-parameter linear contextual bandit under LDP
unmapped: multi-parameter model: shared context X_t in R^d, each arm i has its own parameter theta_i
(epsilon,delta)-local differential privacy constraint, including protection of the pulled arm
diversity condition (Assumption 5) with partition into K_opt and K_sub and gap h_sub for surely-suboptimal arms
the learner knows h_sub, gamma, beta, kappa_l, p', C_B, c_r (used in warm-up length s_0 and elimination threshold h)
settings.definition_quote:
The regret over time horizon $T$ is $\text{Reg}(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \left( \mu(X_{t}^T \theta^{\star}_{a_t^{*}}) - \mu(X_{t}^T \theta^{\star}_{a_t})\right)$. 
If we don't assume any structure on $\{\theta^{\star}_i\}_{i\in [K]}$, we refer it as the multi-parameter setting.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-parameter generalized linear contextual bandit under LDP
unmapped: multi-parameter model: shared context X_t, separate parameter theta_i per arm, reward mu(X_t^T theta_i)
epsilon-local differential privacy constraint, including protection of the pulled arm
diversity condition (Assumption 5) with gap h_sub for surely-suboptimal arms
the learner knows h_sub, kappa_l, p', K_opt and zeta (step size) and C_B, c_r
settings.definition_quote:
We consider the generalized linear bandits by allowing $v(X_t, a_t) = \mu(X_t^T\theta^{\star}_{a_t})$, where $\mu:\R\to \R$ is a link function and $\theta^{\star}_i\in\R^d$ is the underlying parameter of the $i$-th arm. For a fix time t, we denote $a^{*}_t = \argmax_{i\in [K]} \mu(X_{t}^T \theta^{\star}_i)$.
The regret over time horizon $T$ is $\text{Reg}(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \left( \mu(X_{t}^T \theta^{\star}_{a_t^{*}}) - \mu(X_{t}^T \theta^{\star}_{a_t})\right)$. 
If we don't assume any structure on $\{\theta^{\star}_i\}_{i\in [K]}$, we refer it as the multi-parameter setting.
